title: Semantics as a Shield: Label Disguise Defense (LDD) against Prompt Injection in LLM Sentiment Classification
abstract: arXiv:2511.21752v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Prompt injection can cause large language models (LLMs) to deviate from their intended tasks by following instructions embedded in untrusted input. We investigate whether changing a classifier's output labels improves accuracy under such attacks, using sentiment classification as a case study. Label Disguise Defense (LDD) replaces positive/negative with alternatives such as good/bad or cat/dog, introduced through demonstrations, and maps predictions back to sentiment classes. We analyze retained aggregate results for 200 IMDb reviews, nine recorded model configurations, and eight alternative label pairs under a fixed attack that always requests the incorrect class using the original labels. Averaged over four pairs per group, sentiment-associated labels outperform the other tested labels in all nine configurations, but exceed a baseline using the original labels and the same demonstration and attack conditions in only three. translated_title: 语义作为盾牌：针对大语言模型情感分类中提示注入攻击的标签伪装防御（LDD）
translated_abstract: 提示注入攻击可以通过让大语言模型（LLM）遵循嵌入在不可信输入中的指令，使其偏离预期任务。我们以情感分类作为案例研究，探讨改变分类器的输出标签能否在此类攻击下提高准确性。标签伪装防御（LDD）用替代标签（如好/坏或猫/狗）替换正面/负面标签，通过示例引入这些标签，并将预测结果映射回情感类别。我们在固定攻击条件下（该攻击始终使用原始标签请求错误类别）分析了200条IMDb影评的保留聚合结果、九个已记录的模型配置以及八组替代标签对。对每组四对标签取平均值后，与情感相关的标签在全部九个配置中都优于其他测试标签，但仅在三个配置中超过了使用原始标签及相同示例和攻击条件的基线。
tldr: 该论文提出标签伪装防御（LDD）方法，通过将情感分类的输出标签替换为替代标签（如好/坏或猫/狗）来抵御提示注入攻击，实验表明与情感相关的替代标签在全部九个模型配置中均优于其他测试标签，但仅在三个配置中超过使用原始标签的基线。
